subject: Quillon Health - ephemeral log erasement & key rotation clarification
messages:
From: Alex Dunn <alex.dunn@quillonhealth.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>

Subject: Quillon - ephemeral logs / deletion proof for auditors

Hi Irene,

Quick follow-up from the security assessment: our auditors are asking for two pieces from Redwood for tenant-scoped session/debug logs tied to our Quillon environment:

1) Confirmation of the default retention window for ephemeral session and request-level debug logs for hosted tenants, and whether that retention can be shortened at the tenant level (Quillon would like to reduce to 14 days if possible).

2) A described mechanism & artifact for "proof of deletion" once logs are purged—specifically, whether Redwood can provide a deletion manifest or signed statement (hash or audit entry) that shows when tenant-scoped blobs/objects were removed.

Separately: our security team needs clarification on keystore rotation: we use customer-managed KMS for a subset of keys. Can you confirm rotation cadence you enforce for Redwood-managed tenant keys vs. customer-managed keys, and whether rotation events are included in exportable audit logs?

We realize some of this may differ between Hosted / Dedicated / Private, so a short table + an attestation template would be ideal for the audit. Can you also confirm if customer-specific retention exceptions (longer holds) require a signed amendment and Security/Legal approval?

If easier, would love a 30-minute sync this week to walk auditors through the artifacts.

Thanks,
Alex Dunn
Security & Compliance
Quillon Health
attachments: none

Subject: Re: Quillon - ephemeral logs / deletion proof for auditors

Alex — thanks for the clear list. See answers below (short-form) and I attached a compact matrix and key-rotation summary for your auditors.

On Thu, Jun 18, 2026 at 9:12 AM Alex Dunn <alex.dunn@quillonhealth.com> wrote:
> 1) retention window for ephemeral session and request-level debug logs
> 2) proof of deletion artifact
> 3) keystore rotation cadence and auditability

Summary answers (hosted / dedicated / private):
- Default ephemeral session/debug logs (hosted): 21 days. This is the production baseline we operate to for hosted API customers.
- Dedicated: default is 30 days but configurable by contract.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): retention is customer-controlled; Redwood provides the retention tooling and deletion hooks but the customer typically owns the final disposition.

Tenant-level changes: for Hosted we can approve tenant-specific reductions (eg, Quillon -> 14 days) operationally without code changes; this requires a ticket + signed CSA addendum for change-of-retention if it deviates from contractually committed SLAs. For increases/holds beyond baseline we require engagement with Legal/Security and an executed amendment (see below).

Proof-of-delete options we can provide:
- Deletion audit log entries exported as CSV/JSON showing object id, tenant id, deletion timestamp, operator id, and deletion reason.
- A post-delete manifest: SHA256 list for objects removed during a purge window, signed by Redwood's audit key (HSM-backed). This is generated on request for compliance windows; note: manifests are retained for the audit retention window only.
- If you need forensic-level certificates of deletion we can coordinate a short export (secure transfer) that includes the above plus a server-side retention/GC trace.

Keystore rotation & auditability:
- Redwood-managed tenant keys (hosted): primary rotation cadence is 90 days by default; operational rotation occurs more frequently for platform keys and after critical events. Rotation events are logged to the security audit stream and are exportable.
- Customer-managed KMS: rotation cadence is up to the customer; Redwood records KMS key change events in our audit log when we see them (we do not rotate customer-managed keys).
- For HSM integrations we can provide signed rotation events (timestamp + signing key id) as part of the audit bundle.

Exceptions & approval path:
- Customer-specific hold/extension (eg, extend retention to support forensics) requires Security + Legal signoff and a short amendment. We can provision temporary holds (30–180 days) by exception while the amendment is processed in urgent cases.

Next steps proposed:
1) I attached a small log-retention-matrix.csv and keystore-rotation-overview.pdf that map hosted/dedicated/private semantics.
2) If Quillon wants the 14-day tenant reduction for hosted, please confirm the request in writing and we will open a change ticket (no impact to production).
3) If you want a deletion manifest for the last quarterly purge, confirm the date window and we will produce the signed SHA256 manifest and deletion-export.

I can join a 30-min sync tomorrow morning (PST) to walk the auditors through the artifacts — Ben (cc) will own the attestation letter if you need one.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Sr. Security & Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference
attachments: log-retention-matrix.csv, keystore-rotation-overview.pdf

Alex — I can take the attestation.

- Attestation we provide will state the baseline retention and the requested tenant-level change (if you confirm) and reference the signed amendment template.
- For the deletion manifest we will include the signed SHA256 manifest and the deletion audit CSV. Expect a digital signature from Redwood's audit key; chain of custody notes will be embedded in the export.
- Timeline: once you confirm the date window we will produce the manifest within 3 business days; the attestation letter (using the attached template) will be sent the same week pending Legal review.

If you want to lock a 30-min slot (Irene + me + Marissa) I have availability tomorrow 10:00–11:00 PST. Otherwise reply here with the exact purge window and whether you want the tenant retention shortened to 14 days.
